text:
Kavya Rao: Short thread to capture runtime Q&A follow-ups and owners from today's all-hands.
Devon Park: Quick sync: are the p95 targets we announced measured with warmed KV cache and which context size? Need to standardize our perf jobs.
Kavya Rao: Yes — targets are steady-state (warmed cache), 8k context profile. Hosted p95 target 120ms, Dedicated committed p95 100ms. We'll publish a cold-start baseline separately.
Lina Morales: Do those numbers assume our quantized default? Some teams are using fp16 for benchmarks.
Kavya Rao: Right — those are for the quantized serving path (int8/4-bit). FP16 typically shows +10-25ms depending on model and hardware.
Harper Jones: Batching: can routing teams override the latency_budget heuristic per-route? We had issues when global dynamic batching was enabled.
Kavya Rao: Yes, per-route overrides supported. Default runtime uses latency-first: flush on max_batch_size or latency_budget_ms, whichever hits first. There's an opt-in throughput tier for routes that tolerate more latency.
Devon Park: Can someone post the smallest runnable config we can paste into our perf runner? Prefer a tiny JSON snippet we can copy.
Kavya Rao: Will post a minimal snippet here tonight. It will include fields: max_batch_size, latency_budget_ms, dynamic_batching_enabled, route_mode.
sre-oncall: Ops question — a customer reported tail spikes when global eviction pressure kicked in. What immediate mitigations are recommended?
Lina Morales: Short term: increase tenant_cache_ttl and lower global_pressure_threshold for the tenant. Long term: move to per-tenant LRU with a protected-recent-prefix slab and adaptive eviction that honors per-tenant QoS.
Kavya Rao: Runtime to publish the eviction algorithm doc and expected metric deltas. Planned metrics: eviction_total, eviction_by_reason, eviction_tenant_ratio, protected_prefix_hits.
Harper Jones: Tracing: to triage hotspots we need kernel-level timing on Console (matmul/attention/softmax). Current traces lump kernels into a single span.
Kavya Rao: Agreed — we'll add kernel spans behind a flag next sprint. Fields: kernel_name, kernel_duration_ms, kernel_device_id. We'll also include a coarse hop-level aggregation to keep trace volume reasonable.
Devon Park: Hotpatch safety follow-up: a recent hotpatch left some requests stalled during the canary. Who should we feed trace ids to?
Kavya Rao: Tag SRE+Runtime here and drop them. Runtime will prioritize reproducing and hardening rollback-handshake.
Devon Park: example traces: trace-2026-12-22-9 and trace-2026-12-22-12.
deploy-bot: deployment: runtime/kernel-aot-proto -> canary group sigma (job 12456) :rocket:
sre-oncall: We'll watch p95/p99 and kernel_failure_rate during the canary window. Tag release-war-room for escalation.
Lina Morales: ETA on AOT/vectorized attention kernels? Teams want rough perf expectations to plan rollouts.
Kavya Rao: Timeline: design 2w, prototype 3w, early canary 3-4w. Expect initial p95 reductions in the mid-teens percent for long-context models; we'll publish numbers after the prototype run.
Harper Jones: Can we get a short rollout readiness checklist for teams? I want to make sure product routes are ready.
Kavya Rao: Yes 
Checklist (short): 1) run compatibility test against AOT prototype; 2) run eval suite and compare output diffs; 3) validate any custom ops; 4) prepare per-route batch overrides; 5) enable canary flag + monitor kernel_failure_rate, eviction_total, p95/p99. Will post a copy-paste checklist.
Kavya Rao: Actions captured: Runtime to publish eviction doc + kernel-span flag; Kavya to post config snippet and checklist; SRE to monitor canary metrics and triage hang traces; Devon to run local perf tests once snippet posted. Ping me if I missed anything.
Devon Park: I'll follow up in #eng-runtime with test results once I have the snippet.
Harper Jones: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
